recipes.title: Pet activity monitor
recipes.summary: A photo-based activity tally with explicit gaps, plus an offline control card.

support.released: unknown; compare public changes and installed health
support.requirements: GET /v1/health, /v1/capabilities and installed /v1/guide must confirm every operation and grant. Source support alone is insufficient.

phone: Timer → bounded camera snapshot → free local change filter → Clef choice → persistent watch tally → HTML card reads tally and state.
The phone continues watching with the controller offline; remote model inference still needs internet. Pausing preserves the tally and does not extend expiry.
controller: Create the watch and save the returned watch_id. To point the card at it, replace "resource_id":null inside the card's /*RECIPE*/ ... /*END RECIPE*/ block with "resource_id":"<watch_id>" before posting card_request.

The no-meal rule fires on the phone at 18:00 local phone time. In the installed package it runs the Dinner check flow (photo of the bowl, Clef says full, eaten from or not in view, then the matching notice); the card's Check bowl now runs the same flow. The flow needs Jev and Clef questions on in Agent permissions (off by default; the install review lists it). In the plain watch it posts the notice directly. To reach an owner who is away from the phone, also read the watch.rule event (callback_url or GET /v1/events) and pass it to the owner's own chat, or use native Pet Monitor's portal (see boundaries).
Changes to the watch definition require snapshotting the old tally, stopping it, and recreating; the new watch has a new tally.
execution.server: Only explicit decision-model/weather requests leave the phone; direct or relay transport still requires a running reachable phone.

boundaries: Public composition is a generic watch, not the native Pet Monitor. It does not inherit native camera selection, dual-model comparisons, pet history/portal, microphone classifier, camera search or feeding.
Samples show visible activity only. A missed pet is unknown coverage; cached classifications are reused evidence, not new model observations.

A generic watch shows results on the phone itself (cards, speech) and to its controlling agent. A remote web view for the owner exists only for the native Pet Monitor (see https://bridgit.cc/learn/applet-backends.md).

lifecycle.start: POST /v1/watches with the start example; retain the returned watch_id. Then render/post the card with resource_id.
lifecycle.update: GET state/tally first. To change the definition, export required history, DELETE old watch, POST revised definition. No watch PATCH exists.
lifecycle.pause: POST /v1/watches/{id}/pause with {"paused":true}; resume with false. Confirm user_paused from the returned metadata. Expiry is unchanged.
lifecycle.stop: DELETE /v1/watches/{id}; confirm deleted equals the saved id and watch.ended reason deleted. Archive needed tally BEFORE deletion. Cancel the interaction separately.

failure: Camera locked/busy: record an error gap and retry at a later slot; never classify it as resting.
Budget/quota/model failure: inspect recent_checks and watch.ended. The template never turns an unavailable reading into zero episodes.
cost: The installed package's Dinner check adds at most 10 paid Clef calls a day (one photo each), whether the 18:00 rule or Check bowl now starts it.

At most 10 paid Clef calls an hour for this watch. Worst case, running all day every day, that is about 7,200 photos and $0.76 a month at Clef's ~$0.000105 a photo. That fits the default monthly budget ($1.50, shared by all the phone's agents); budgets differ per account, so read GET /v1/limits and scale max_paid_per_hour to the real value. Unchanged scenes reuse the last answer for free, so real use is usually much lower.

Clef's free allowance (about 970 photos a day) is shared by all of Bridgit: keep the change check on and the cap low. Check usage.paid_cost_usd and skipped_over_paid_cap; a quiet scene still refreshes within 900 seconds.
extensions: Use an enrolled lan:<id> camera after grant checks.
Tune episode gaps and confidence with labeled samples before interpreting totals.
Add a no-water rule ({fewer_than:1, of:"drinking", by:"18:00"}) or a none_for_s rule for long gaps between meals.

support.released: unknown; compare public changes and installed health
support.requirements: GET /v1/health, /v1/capabilities and installed /v1/guide must confirm every operation and grant, and the installed API revision must be at least 71 (situation in POST /v1/watches). Source support alone is insufficient.

phone: Timer → camera → free local change check → Clef yes/no on changed photos → episode tally on the phone → watch.matched event and, for alert situations, an urgent owner notice.
The phone expands situation into the tuned question, the tally (track = the situation id, or "situation" for own words) and the alert rule; unchanged photos reuse the last answer for free.
controller: Optional: read GET /v1/watches/{id}/tally to archive day totals; the card and the count work with no agent.
Pick the situation with the owner: a library id from GET /v1/situations or the owner's own words.
execution.server: Only Clef photo checks leave the phone (model left out, so Clef is the default for a camera watch); direct or relay transport still requires a running reachable phone.

boundaries: A count is sampled photos judged by a model, not continuous coverage or proof: gaps, a locked camera or the thing being out of frame are unknown, not zero.
It does not diagnose health or detect fire: a smoke or boiling-over count is a nudge, not a safety alarm.

lifecycle.start: POST /v1/watches with the start example; retain the returned watch_id. Then render/post the card with resource_id.

lifecycle.stop: DELETE /v1/watches/{id}; confirm deleted equals the saved id and watch.ended reason deleted. Archive needed tally BEFORE deletion. Cancel the interaction separately.

failure: Own words that look like an id (lowercase_with_underscores) but aren't in the library are refused: describe it with spaces instead.
A busy or locked camera is a gap; poor light, glare and odd angles cause misses and false counts. Aim the camera and try a known example first.
cost: Clef photo checks from the phone's model budget: at most max_paid_per_hour (30 here, under the 50-an-hour limit some phones have) an hour; unchanged pictures reuse the last answer for free. Read GET /v1/limits and lower the cap or lengthen interval_s for long runs.
extensions: Send {"situation": {"describe": "...", "alert": true}} to count own words and notify the owner when one starts.

card.owner_intro: Counts how often the camera sees one situation today.
card.owner_note: Sampled photos judged by a model. Gaps and things out of frame are unknown, and it is not a safety alarm.

start.fits: Spot and count a common picture situation on the camera: a pot boiling over, smoke, water on the floor, the dog licking or scratching itself, the dog on the couch, the cat on the counter, sunlight in the room, lights left on, or one described in the owner's words.

you_decide.question: Which situation should the camera count: a library id (GET /v1/situations) or the owner's own words?
you_decide.default: pot_boiling_over with the back camera every 20 seconds (the start example); own words go in situation as a sentence with spaces.

first_calls: GET /v1/capabilities
GET /v1/limits
GET /v1/situations

POST /v1/applets/validate {"url":"https://bridgit.cc/recipes/situation-counter/applet.json","config":{"situation":"<a library id or the owner's words>"}}: read review (what the owner will see), warnings and package
POST /v1/applets/install with the same body (needs your Install applets permission); the owner approves once on the phone; wait for applet.installed (with instance_id) in GET /v1/events

Only if you lack Install applets: POST /v1/watches with examples[start] (situation set to the owner's pick); save watch_id; then POST /v1/interactions with card_request from recipe_url, resource_id set to watch_id
start.adapt: Set situation to the library id or the owner's words; leave question, questions and tally out (the phone fills them in). Alert situations (pot_boiling_over, smoke_in_room, water_on_floor) also send the owner an urgent notice when an episode starts; {"id": ..., "alert": false} turns that off. Set max_paid_per_hour from GET /v1/limits and use the library's interval_s for slow situations (sunlight, lights: 300). To change it: fill other blanks in config, or fetch the applet.json, edit it (card pieces, flows, tables) and send it as {"package": …}; validate returns the complete file.
done_when: applet.installed arrived and GET /v1/applets/installed shows it active
